references.context: Set theory: power set of an arbitrary underlying set X, namely the collection of all subsets of X; variable names X and S are interchangeable.
references.matching_note: Consolidated original notation 'power set P(X)' into the same set-theoretic power-set concept; no suitably typed meaning occurs among existing meanings.

references.phrase: empty set and whole-set membership in tau
references.disposition: These are the defining nullary topology axioms ∅∈τ and X∈τ; the abstract empty set and set membership are background foundational notation, not separate topology-dependent definitions.

references.context: Set theory: union ⋃_{i∈I}U_i of a possibly infinite indexed family of subsets of X, including empty-index union ∅; the requirement that this union belong to τ is an axiom defining a topology.
references.reason: An indexed set union is a reusable operation separately from the topology's closure axiom.
references.matching_note: Typed source-free provisional set-union prerequisite; retain topology axiom versus general set operation distinction.

references.context: Set theory: intersection ⋂_{i∈F}U_i of finitely many subsets of ambient X, including the empty-index intersection X; topology requires this intersection to lie in τ.
references.reason: Finite intersections are a set operation used as an input to, not equivalent to, the topology closure axiom.
references.matching_note: Typed source-free provisional finite-intersection operation; compare to set intersections elsewhere only after contextual review.

references.disposition: Open sets are defined by membership in tau, not imported from metric-space openness or a nonempty-space convention.
references.phrase: members of tau are open subsets

references.context: Set theory: relative complement A\B={x∈A:x∉B} for two sets A,B⊆X; in the sigma-algebra axiom A,B are members of Σ.
references.reason: Relative set difference is a standalone construction separate from the condition that Σ be closed under it.
references.matching_note: Do not confuse with symmetric difference or ring subtraction.

references.context: Set theory: pairwise disjoint indexed set family (A_i), satisfying A_i∩A_j=∅ for all distinct indices i,j.
references.reason: Pairwise disjointness is reusable set-family structure beyond the sigma-algebra it helps define.
references.matching_note: Keep distinct from mutually independent random variables or disjoint indexed union notation.

references.phrase: countable union of pairwise disjoint members
references.context: Set theory: countable indexed union ⋃_{n∈N}A_n of sets, here drawn from a pairwise-disjoint family; the sigma-algebra clause requires the union to remain a member of Σ.
references.reason: The countable-family union construction is a prerequisite; membership in Σ is only the defining closure axiom.
references.matching_note: Potential overlap with arbitrary set union and pairwise-disjoint family: inspect compound occurrence in global audit rather than automatically aliasing.

references.disposition: The ambient-set membership condition is an axiom; the equivalent formulation need not list arbitrary countable-union closure explicitly.
This form supplies equivalent axioms of the same sigma-algebra concept and must not have an artificial definition dependency upon its own meaning.

references.context: General topology: indexed family (U_i) of open subsets of X with ⋃_i U_i=X, allowing arbitrary index set; no Hausdorff requirement.
references.reason: The open-cover construction is independently useful and presupposed by the compactness condition.
references.matching_note: Do not require each cover to be finite or nonempty when the underlying space is empty.

references.context: General topology: finite subfamily of a given open cover (U_i)_{i∈I} indexed by finite F⊆I such that ⋃_{i∈F}U_i=X; the existence of one for every cover defines compactness.
references.reason: A finite subcover is a reusable structure of a cover, not the compactness predicate itself.
references.matching_note: For X=∅ the empty finite subcover is allowed in the usual convention.

references.disposition: Compactness in this formulation does not include separation axioms.

references.phrase: compact topological space via open covers

references.context: General set theory/topology: family (F_i) of subsets of X with ⋂_{i∈E}F_i nonempty for every nonempty finite E of indices; specify the empty-family convention separately.
references.reason: The finite-intersection property is a standalone family property used in the closed-set compactness characterization.
references.matching_note: Empty family conventions and empty topological space need global audit to avoid a false compactness equivalence.

references.disposition: The consequence ⋂_iF_i≠∅ is precisely the defining compactness characterization under the finite-intersection-property hypothesis, not an independently presupposed named construction. Set intersection itself is addressed by other references.
Complementation of covers gives the equivalent criterion with no Hausdorff assumption.

references.phrase: subset tau of the power set of X
generated sigma-algebra from open family tau
references.context: Measure theory: σ-algebra σ(𝒜) generated by an arbitrary family 𝒜⊆P(X), the least σ-algebra on X containing 𝒜; Borel case specializes to 𝒜=τ.
references.reason: Generation of a sigma-algebra from a family is a reusable construction independent of the particular Borel sigma-algebra being defined.
references.matching_note: Separate generic generated σ-algebra from the same Borel object; global cycle/alias audit required.

references.phrase: intersection of all containing sigma algebras
references.disposition: This is the explicit intersection construction establishing the least σ-algebra containing τ, a defining equivalent expression for the Borel σ-algebra. Do not insert a self-dependency upon Borel or a second generated-σ-algebra identity.
The topology tau is essential input; Borel sigma-algebra is not generally the full power set.
